---
title: "Accessibility"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
```

`accessibility()` summarises, for each origin, how many opportunities (jobs,
schools, hospitals...) can be reached, either counting those within a time
limit or weighting every one of them by how long it takes to get there. The
travel times come from the same computation as `travel_time_matrix()`.

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.alt = "Accessibility is the sum over destinations of the opportunities times a weight that decays with the travel time; five decay functions are drawn for a 30 minute cutoff: step, exponential, fixed exponential, linear and logistic."}
fig("accessibility.svg")
```

Two details make the results match r5r's to the last bit: the travel time fed
to the decay function is the percentile in **seconds**, not rounded to minutes
as in the matrix, and the exponentials are computed with the same algorithm
as R5 (Apache Commons Math's `FastMath.exp`), not with the C library's.

## Cumulative opportunities

The `"step"` function counts the opportunities reached in less than each
cutoff. Each origin gets one row per opportunity column, percentile and
cutoff:

```{r}
access <- accessibility(
  network, points, points,
  opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools"),
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = departure,
  decay_function = "step",
  cutoffs = c(15, 30),
  percentiles = c(25, 75),
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
head(access, 8)
```

As in r5r, with `"step"` trips longer than the largest cutoff are not routed
at all (`max_trip_duration` becomes `max(cutoffs)`), and `max_trip_duration`
may not be shorter than the largest cutoff with any function.

## Decay functions

The other functions weight every opportunity by its travel time. Their
`decay_value` means different things: the width of the ramp in minutes for
`"linear"`, the standard deviation in minutes for `"logistic"`, the decay
constant per second for `"fixed_exponential"`; `"exponential"` uses the cutoff
as its half-life.

```{r}
one <- function(fun, value = NULL, cutoffs = 20) {
  a <- accessibility(
    network, points[1:3, ], points,
    opportunities_colnames = "jobs",
    mode = "WALK",
    decay_function = fun, decay_value = value, cutoffs = cutoffs,
    n_threads = 2
  )
  setNames(round(a$accessibility), a$id)
}
rbind(
  step = one("step"),
  exponential = one("exponential"),
  linear = one("linear", 10),
  logistic = one("logistic", 5),
  fixed_exponential = one("fixed_exponential", 0.001, cutoffs = NULL)
)
```

`"fixed_exponential"` ignores cutoffs, so `cutoffs` must be `NULL` and the
result has no `cutoff` column.

## Street modes

Any street mode works too; the times are then the same for every percentile.

```{r}
by_bike <- accessibility(
  network, points, points,
  opportunities_colnames = "jobs",
  mode = "BICYCLE",
  decay_function = "logistic", decay_value = 5, cutoffs = 15,
  n_threads = 2
)
summary(by_bike$accessibility)
```

## Missing counts

Missing opportunity counts count as zero, with a warning, as in r5r:

```{r}
holes <- points
holes$jobs[2] <- NA
a <- accessibility(network, points[1, ], holes,
                   opportunities_colnames = "jobs", mode = "WALK",
                   decay_function = "step", cutoffs = 30, n_threads = 2)
a
```
